reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the core mechanism: it identifies fast nanosegregation as the cause of ductility loss, demonstrates that preexisting Cr-rich precipitates absorb embrittling elements and prevent intergranular cracking, and shows improved ductility in a dual-phase variant at 600–700°C. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings, though the specific intervention (minor Cr addition + aging) and the predicted 20–30% toughness enhancement are extrapolations not directly tested in the cited work.
premises: Ductility loss in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi at intermediate temperatures is due to intergranular cracking caused by fast nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, Mn to grain boundaries.
Preexisting Cr-rich precipitates at grain boundaries can act as sinks for these embrittling elements.
Redirecting segregation into Cr-rich precipitates prevents grain boundary decohesion and evades ductility loss.
A dual-phase HEA with Cr-rich precipitates shows greater ductility than a single-phase HEA at 600–700°C and no intergranular embrittlement.
Deliberately introducing Cr-rich nano-precipitates via minor Cr addition and aging will reproduce this protective effect in a modified CrMnFeCoNi alloy.
